content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Link several weekly habits with and, but, and because. Model: “I usually cook at home, but I eat with friends on Friday.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use a balanced weekly routine clearly and politely. One useful response is: “I usually cook at home, but I eat with friends on Friday.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where a balanced weekly routine is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

exercises.prompt: Complete the natural sentence about a balanced weekly routine: I usually cook at home, but I eat with friends _____.

I eat with friends on Friday
items: I eat with friends on Friday

exercises.prompt: Put these two parts in a natural order to make a message about a balanced weekly routine.
Make a short, personal response about a balanced weekly routine. Use the lesson language and add one detail that is yours.

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about a balanced weekly routine.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.
The response adds an appropriate personal or invented detail.

language_focus: Link several weekly habits with and, but, and because.
objectives: Link several weekly habits with and, but, and because.
Use present-simple integration in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about a balanced weekly routine.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about a balanced weekly routine. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: Why does the speaker eat out on Friday?
listening.transcript: I usually cook on Monday, but I eat out on Friday because I meet friends.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Pause lightly before but and because; stress FRIENDS. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Pause lightly before but and because; stress FRIENDS.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about a balanced weekly routine.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using a balanced weekly routine; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise a balanced weekly routine?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: I usually cook at home, but I eat with friends on Friday.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about a balanced weekly routine with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about a balanced weekly routine. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: I usually cook at home, but I eat with friends on Friday. Submit your draft first.
